summary: The retrieval literature supports making useful repository relationships legible to agents, but the exact structural prescription remains an engineering hypothesis that must be measured locally.

points.text: Use task success, retrieval precision, context size and time-to-orientation to test whether a project map, naming rule or ADR index actually improves agent work.
A clean directory tree is only a proxy for semantic relevance. Cross-cutting behavior, generated code and runtime configuration often violate folder boundaries.
Instruction files and architecture maps become harmful when stale: their authoritative tone can cause an agent to prefer obsolete context over executable evidence.
